title: The whole price
question: Laura's Room's paragraph answers the strongest rival by name (same ladder, stocks until 2031) and prices our 2028 floor at 'about $9,000 of her own money in a typical 2033'. Is that the whole price, is the paragraph clear and in our voice, and should it replace V45's 'Sell low, by appointment'?
serves: North stars 3 and 4 (extraordinary; investing knowledge applied: a priced insurance trade-off) and Commandments V, IV, III; Investment Strategy and Portfolio Analysis (the trade-offs, 'under varying market outcomes')
essence: We argued over whether owning Laura's gift floor from 2028 costs her about $9,000, as the paragraph said; in our model it is nearer $19,000 on average by 2042, because the rival plan usually wins.

We kept the plan and rewrote the paragraph to say so: the rival usually wins by about $19,000, but in the worst one in twenty markets it has to sell stocks in a slump and names about $90,000 to co-sponsors against our $140,000. Six blind judges preferred that version, and a voice reader ranked it above the plain repair.
The next draft can answer the rival a growth-minded judge would have written, with an honest price, instead of beating a 60/40 four judges called a straw man.
decided: 5-0 (Jun absent): LR-08's paragraph AMENDED and promoted as LR3 to the rewrite inbox, replacing V45's heading and both 60/40 paragraphs; 497 strict

3-1 (Felix abstained): the rival 'sells stocks in January 2031, whatever they fetch that morning' (Kai) and 'after the 2031 set-aside' (Tess) go in; 'leaves her over $40,000 behind' goes to the Final Report to pay for them
Price stated as a mean, by 2042 ($19,000, house world), not the $9,000 median of 2033 (C-04)
Voice gate passed: blind reader ranks LR3 above LR2; V45's paragraph is still first on voice
seeds: Can the January-morning image be called back in the 'But' sentence ('that January morning arrives mid-slump') within 497?
Does 'ten one-year bills' belong anywhere in the IPS once the rival also owns the ladder?
